name: HF Sinclair Corp
moat_justification: A price-taking commodity refiner whose 2026 windfall was handed to it by geopolitics, not earned by any durable advantage; its real edges are locational and logistical (inland refinery placement, complexity, integration), which soften the cycle but have never repealed it — OE was negative as recently as FY2021 and the 2022 peak OE total is roughly 4x the FY2025 figure.
fragility_flags: STALE_FY: latest fiscal year ended 9 months ago — check TTM/quarterly OE and consider --base-oe-ps override
BUYBACK_TAILWIND: share count shrinking 2.7%/yr — already credited via the growth adjustment
BASIS_BREAK_SUSPECT: a >60% revenue jump/drop in the last 5 yrs — check for divestitures, big M&A, or restatements before trusting any CAGR
OE_VOLATILE: OE/share range over the last 5 yrs spans >3x — normalized base helps but the business is cyclical; widen bear weight
NI_OCF_DIVERGENCE: net income and operating cash flow differ by >40% in 2024 — find the one-off (tax deposits, impairments, WC swings) before trusting the OE base
one_liner: Peak-cycle refiner, moat 3/10 — war-driven crack spreads handed it a $12.65 TTM OE/share, but on the normalized $4.47 base the weighted IRR is 5.22% (IV@15% $28.25 vs $124.80); it clears 15% only at ~$28 or below.
moat_for: Complex, flexible refineries in advantaged inland regions capturing discounted inland crude differentials
Integrated midstream, marketing and the Sinclair brand dampen pure spot-refining exposure
Lubricants & Specialties is a steadier, higher-margin business (top-5 North America); H2 2027 spin-off could surface value
Modest leverage — net debt 2.15x normalized OE — so downcycles are survivable
moat_against: Pure price-taker on crude and products; crack spreads set by global supply/demand and geopolitics
No pricing power, switching costs or network effects in commodity fuels
Capital-intensive: turnaround and environmental capex run near D&A over a cycle
Subscale versus Marathon Petroleum, Phillips 66 and Valero
Long-term US gasoline demand decline from EVs and fuel-economy gains
